title: Backprop through time, and a cell
summary: Why a plain recurrent net loses long gradients, and what an LSTM changes.

choices.text: Once a network is an LSTM, the gradient through time cannot vanish for any setting of the gates. The memory is permanent.
Exploding gradients are commonly handled by clipping the gradient. Clipping does not restore a gradient that has already vanished.
Backpropagation through time unrolls the recurrent net and applies the chain rule along that path. A shared weight gets a gradient summed over the time steps that used it.

An LSTM cell is updated as forget-gate times old cell, plus an input term. A forget gate near 1 leaves a path whose multiplier is near 1, instead of the same squashing matrix every step, which is how the cell carries a dependency further.

A vanilla RNN multiplies by the same recurrent matrix every step. If the singular values of that matrix sit well below 1, repeated products vanish; if they sit well above 1, products can explode. Either way a long-range gradient is fragile.
